title: The Thing
synopsis: An Antarctic research station, a Norwegian helicopter, and a thing that imitates anything it touches.

nodes.text: A helicopter hunts a dog across white tundra with a rifle. You cannot avoid Camp Dog; you can only decide whether “Take cover” or “Shoot back” defines the person who reaches it. By Camp Dog, the danger will have learned what you protect first.

choices.consequence: You commit to take cover. It carries you into Camp Dog while the safer possibility closes without making a sound.
You choose to shoot back. By Camp Dog, the danger will know a little more about you than you know about it.

nodes.text: A bottle of scotch, a fire, a long silence in the wind. “Drink” draws you toward Wait for the Cold; “Wait” leaves Test Passed waiting on the other side. A third choice, “Take the third path,” keeps The Thing Walks in play.

Some endings reveal themselves last. You take the third path. The way toward The Thing Walks opens, and something on the other side seems to notice.

nodes.text: You sit across from Childs with a flask between you and you watch each other for tells while the fire dies, and you wait for the dawn or the end. The road into Wait for the Cold began with “Drink” in Two Men in the Snow; here, that decision stops being a moment and becomes a life.

You both come up clean. The next research team finds you sleeping back-to-back in the wreckage. The road into Test Passed began with “Wait” in Two Men in the Snow; here, that decision stops being a moment and becomes a life.

One of you is wrong. The other one doesn't know it yet. The wind takes the bottle. The story does not end. The road into The Thing Walks began with “Take the third path” in Two Men in the Snow; here, that decision stops being a moment and becomes a life.
